docs.title: Open-source security libraries for PHP
docs.text: The documentation of each library: what it does, the specifications it implements, how to install it and where to ask about it.

docs.title: The frameworks
docs.text:
What an application installs for what it does: who the user is, what they may do, and the tokens and certificates that carry the answer.

Authentication WebAuthn Framework WebAuthn and passkeys for PHP and Symfony. web-auth/webauthn-lib Tokens JWT Framework JSON Web Tokens for PHP and Symfony: signature (JWS), encryption (JWE) and keys (JWK). web-token/jwt-framework One-time passwords OTPHP TOTP and HOTP one-time passwords, after RFC 6238 and RFC 4226. spomky-labs/otphp Authorization Access Control Framework Authorization for PHP and Symfony: decides whether a requester is allowed to perform an action on a subject. spomky-labs/access-control-lib Certificates PKI Framework X.509 certificates, ASN.1 and public key infrastructure. spomky-labs/pki-framework

docs.title: For Symfony applications
docs.text:
Bundles that hand an application a capability of the web platform, configured rather than written.

Progressive web apps PWA Bundle Progressive web apps for Symfony: manifest, service worker and offline support. spomky-labs/pwa-bundle Notifications Web Push Framework Web push notifications for PHP and Symfony. spomky-labs/web-push-lib

docs.title: The building blocks
docs.text:
The encoding and the cryptography the frameworks above stand on. Composer installs them for you; their documentation is here for the day you read a stack trace or write a layer of your own.

CBOR PHP CBOR encoding and decoding, after RFC 8949. spomky-labs/cbor-php COSE COSE signing, encryption and key management, after RFC 9052 and RFC 9053. web-auth/cose-lib

docs.title: Security
docs.text: A vulnerability is reported privately, never in a public issue. The security page says how, and lists the published advisories of each library with the versions that fix them.

docs.title: Reporting a vulnerability
docs.text:
A security problem is never reported in a public issue, pull request or discussion: that hands it to every user of the library before a fix exists. Report it privately, either way:

  • with the form Report a vulnerability of the Security tab of the repository, which opens a private thread with the maintainers;
  • by email to security@spomky-labs.com.

The security policy of each repository, SECURITY.md, says which release lines receive fixes.

docs.title: Knowing that a version is affected
docs.text:
Every advisory is published on the repository of its library, then enters the GitHub Advisory Database and the advisories that Packagist serves. From there:

  • composer audit lists the installed packages that an advisory names;
  • Composer refuses such a version on composer update and composer require, by default since Composer 2.9;
  • Dependabot alerts a repository on GitHub whose lock file holds one.

docs.title: The advisories of each library
docs.text:
Library Package WebAuthn Framework web-auth/webauthn-lib and the packages of its repository JWT Framework web-token/jwt-library and the packages of its repository OTPHP spomky-labs/otphp PKI Framework spomky-labs/pki-framework CBOR PHP spomky-labs/cbor-php COSE web-auth/cose-lib

The other libraries, Access Control Framework, PWA Bundle and Web Push Framework, have no published advisory.

docs.text:
The published advisories of Spomky-Labs/cbor-php, the newest first. Each one names the packages and the version ranges it affects. The latest release of every supported line carries every fix.

2026-11-08 RSA private key recoverable through a timing side channel in RSA-OAEP and RSA1_5 decryption High 3.4.13, 4.0.9, 4.1.11, 4.2.6no fix for web-token/jwt-core 2026-10-31 ECDH-ES derives at most 256 bits of key material: with A256CBC-HS512 the content is encrypted under an all-zero AES key and anyone holding the token can read it High 3.4.12, 4.0.8, 4.1.10, 4.2.4no fix for web-token/jwt-encryption-algorithm-ecdh-es 2026-10-31 AES-GCM decryption accepts any authentication tag length: a holder of one valid JWE can brute force a 1-byte tag in at most 256 requests and
